text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation, can you describe the specific characteristics of the skin lesion you are concerned about, such as its size, color, and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the chronic, non-healing nature of these lesions and your significant smoking history, I need to assess for risk factors for squamous cell carcinoma. Are either of these lesions painful, do they bleed easily when touched, and have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your groin or armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No known malignancies or hereditary diseases in the family. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema. Social history: Lives with his 4th wife, smokes 2 packs of cigarettes per day for the last 30 years, has recently immigrated from Africa.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results show features consistent with squamous cell carcinoma in situ, which in this clinical context strongly suggests Erythroplasia of Queyrat on the penis and Bowen's disease on the finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ (Erythroplasia of Queyrat and Bowen's disease)
